For anyone who gets this message, you can stop it from rebooting by starting Task Scheduler, going to Task Scheduler Library/Microsoft/Windows/Update Orchestrator and then right click on the Reboot task and select disable.

If you're on windows 10 Pro or Enterprise you can stop it from rebooting like this permanently by going to Computer Configuration/Administrative Templates/Windows Components/Windows Update in the group policy editor and enabling the rule: No auto restart with loggedon users for scheduled automatic updates installations.

If you have windows 10 home you can use regedit to stop this by going to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU [create the AU folder if its not already there] Create a new DWORD-32 value and name it NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers then edit the key and change the value data to 1.

Note: It seems windows resets this after an update so if you do update then you will have to do it every time, or export the regkey so you can install it each time.

Speaking of hibernate. This is somewhat unrelated but on newer windows operating systems I think from vista onward it has a "hybrid sleep" feature on dekstops that means when your PC sleeps it saves everything in memory like hibernate in the event there is a power outage while its sleeping. It seems that disabling hibernate does not also turn this off meaning if you have a SSD and put your computer into sleep mode a lot you're decreasing its lifespan severely. To turn this off go to Control Panel > Power Options > Edit Plan Settings > Change Advanced Power Settings > Sleep > Allow Hybrid Sleep.
